title: Universal Spin-Position Coupled Rydberg Interactions
abstract: Strong interactions between $s$-orbital Rydberg atoms underpin atom-array-based quantum computation and quantum simulation. Typically, the spin dependence of these interactions is negligible and plays no practical role. In this Letter, we uncover that a strong electron-spin-dependent Rydberg interaction can emerge when the principal quantum numbers of the two $s$-orbital atoms differ by a sweet-spot value. This interaction originates from the fine-structure splitting of nearby $p$ orbitals, which endows it with distinct symmetry properties such that the electron spins are coupled to the relative position of the two atoms, featuring a spatially defined anisotropy. We further demonstrate that this interaction admits a universal form, independent of the principal quantum numbers, and highlight its fundamental distinction from conventional magnetic dipolar interactions, establishing it as a new type of native magnetic interaction in nature. Our findings introduce a new element to the Rydberg quantum simulation toolbox. As a concrete application, we propose a native realization of the Kitaev-Heisenberg model, which hosts an unusual stripe phase as a quantum many-body manifestation of spin-space locking.
summary: This paper uncovers a previously overlooked, universal, and strong electron-spin-dependent interaction in Rydberg atom arrays, arising from fine-structure splitting. This novel interaction possesses unique spin-space locking properties, allowing researchers to engineer the Kitaev-Heisenberg model. The resulting phase diagram predicts a stripe phase, offering a new platform for quantum simulation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the emergence and universal form of strong electron-spin-dependent Rydberg interactions, which are typically ignored in current models of Rydberg atom arrays.
main_result: A universal, spin-dependent Rydberg interaction is found that is fundamentally distinct from conventional dipolar interactions and can realize the Kitaev-Heisenberg model, hosting a novel stripe phase.
method: The analysis combines *ab initio* calculations, symmetry considerations (especially involving fine-structure splitting), and theoretical modeling of lattice Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system is based on arrays of s-orbital Rydberg atoms. The interaction is modeled by a Hamiltonian that includes spin-space locking terms, allowing for the realization of the Kitaev-Heisenberg model on a lattice.
key_observables: Spin-space locking, stripe phases (breaking spin and translational symmetry), and the time evolution of spin states in different relative geometries.
important_parameters: The ratio of detuning ($\Delta E$) to fine-structure splitting ($\Delta f$), and the relative strengths of lattice couplings ($J_x, J_y, J_z$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on symmetry arguments and assumes the dipole-dipole interaction is the primary perturbation channel when $\Delta E \sim \Delta f$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition from spin-independent to spin-dependent interactions, show spin dynamics in different geometries ($R_z, R_x$), and map out the phase diagram of the Kitaev-Heisenberg model, revealing the stripe phase.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical mechanism for the spin-dependent interaction via fine-structure splitting. It then derives the universal Hamiltonian form and applies it to model the Kitaev-Heisenberg model, culminating in a detailed analysis of the resulting phase diagram.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, tunable mechanism within Rydberg arrays to engineer complex, anisotropic magnetic interactions, moving beyond simple van der Waals or purely dipolar couplings.
